P1.evidence: Referenced the pre-call form later in the call — 'I saw that you typed in the chat, like, before our meeting, right, in the form, you mentioned that your belly is getting ridiculous' — which is the P1a move, though delivered at 00:07:10 rather than in the opening. Three-part frame, agreement taken ('Okay. Amazing.'), open question run. Also handled the environment properly, getting the iPad onto a stand.

P2.evidence: Age, weight and height taken; work established properly and its physical nature explored; current training established honestly ('So zero'); diet covered in real detail. Injuries were partially covered — the rep got the knee issue rated 4-5 and probed the mobility rating — but stopped at symptoms. The prospect said 'I know I have just some degenerative life in there' at 00:02:00 and it was never picked up. Health conditions never asked as a category. Energy surfaced only because the prospect volunteered fatigue. Sleep absent.

P3.evidence: The most complete Phase 3 in the batch. Ran the specific physical thing he cannot do (kneeling and getting back up), pushed past 'I don't have a measurement I'm looking for' to what strong actually means to him, asked the bridge question — 'Is there, like, deeper why for you, personally, that you now feel like I need to actually do something?' — and got the answer that carried the call: 'I want to be 80 years old and still be able to whoop my boy's butt.' Then drove it through to the kids explicitly, including the age-gap point about the three-year-old, and reflected it back accurately at 00:33:37 with the prospect confirming 'No, that's it.'

P4.evidence: Established that he had never sought a coach and why, and caught a genuine contradiction well: the prospect said he had plenty of time and also that time was why he had never acted, and the rep challenged it directly — 'do you feel it's, it was more of a time aspect of more priority aspect back then?' That produced the honest answer: 'I don't think I qualified it as a need.' Weaker on making the prospect name a structural gap; 'not having a plan' came from the rep's framing rather than his.

P5.evidence: Run properly for once and prefaced honestly — the rep called out that the prospect had not actually done anything yet, then asked 'what if you don't make the change? And in 10 years from now, nothing really changes... How do you think it would look like at that point?' The answer was reflective rather than fearful and the rep did not press for the cost. No 'willing to settle', no 'why not', no line in the sand. The strongest available material — 'after 15 bales, I got one of the boys to do it for me... that's also part of the decline' — arrived at 00:35:00 and was never used as a consequence lever.

P6.evidence: Belief question asked properly — 'do you feel like if you have all of that in place that you are actually going to become that version of yourself where you are fitter, leaner, and just overall in a better place?' → 'Yeah, absolutely.' The 1-10 returned a genuine 10: 'I would say a ten. Like, that's exactly what I'm after.' But the all-in question was never asked, and it would have surfaced the cash-flow constraint before the price rather than after it — the prospect had already flagged 'I don't have a ton of time' and business seasonality earlier in the call.

P11.evidence: Agreement in principle was reached but the call was interrupted by a family emergency before any step could run. Nothing was collected, booked, signed or sent; a continuation call was set for 2:30pm the same day to do all of it.

objection_plays.detail: Isolation ran twice and ran well — 'if the money aspect, let's say, 6K would just now fall on your lap, would you then be like, yeah, let's just get the ball rolling?' → 'Yeah, if I had to, I'd probably just do it' — and the rep correctly distinguished timing from fear and from value: 'It's a timing piece from what I'm hearing, right? It's not like I don't want to do this, I'm scared to do this.' He then asked the capacity question and got a specific number. What did not run: no monthly surplus, no credit cards, no available credit, no assets, no credit score. The rep took one data point — a $1,000 initial ceiling — and improvised a payment structure on it, then set the first payment 20% above that ceiling.

'I got to put this off for the next 45 days' is a timing objection. The rep ran one OD-adjacent move — 'should we put it off for the next 45 days again?' — which is the right challenge, and the prospect held ('I would need to put it off if I have to spend $6,000, yes'). The rep then solved it commercially rather than with the play. None of the scripted moves ran: no 'things never slow down', no 'the longer you wait the harder this gets', no 'the only thing you can control is right now'.

No scripted path exists for constructing an instalment plan on a call, and it shows. The rep produced a six-term structure with a per-term surcharge in a single garbled sentence, never stated the total, and left the condition for removing the surcharge undefined. The prospect — who had just said he needed to 'process like, how do I do that' — accepted it without a total ever being spoken aloud. This is the gap the internal 1-1 four days earlier described as policy: 'we don't really have any, like... Set payment plans. Everything we do is custom.'

notes: Discovery was the best in the batch — Phase 3 was complete and the 'whoop my boy's butt at 80' material was properly earned. The failure is entirely at the commercial end. The rep diagnosed the objection correctly as timing, then invented a payment structure worth $7,200 in one sentence, above the prospect's stated $1,000 initial ceiling, without ever stating the total. Coachable fix is narrow and specific: state the number of payments, the amount of each and the total, out loud, and confirm it back before asking for agreement.
